notes.title: Cursed Items, Life Renewal, and Inventory Upgrade bunkers
notes.content:
[h1]Alright before I get into this, lemme just rant about some things that have been on my mind[/h1]

I think there has been some confusion going around about what GTTOD is "all about". In the past, I probably would have said some dumb shit like "Lol I dunno man gun shooty go fasty wee wee", confusing everyone and bringing no actual value to the conversation. However, I feel like I've gone long enough without really talking about what I want GTTOD to be - and conversely where I think it is at right now.

SO, the quick version - GTTOD is meant to be a challenging, fast paced, rogue lite shooter. Emphasis on "lite". I never wanted GTTOD to be a full on Rogue Like, nor a generic arena shooter (which is probably why I've always kinda neglected the arena modes lol). I have wanted GTTOD to be more a game about persistence. Fighting against increasingly difficult enemies to loot up and get a cool build going. Getting cool weapons, upgrades, powers and abilities along the way. Fighting to the top of "The Summit" as fast and as hard as you can as to take on the final boss before you become overwhelmed by the difficulty.

To be brazen, I really don't think GTTOD is anywhere NEAR there yet. That's not to say I think GTTOD is "bad". I think right now, the current state of the game is a fun little indie shooter with some movement tech and wacky arenas. But that's not really what I have wanted GTTOD to be...really ever. I think it's a necessary stepping stone on the path to making GTTOD the game that I want it to be. I need to have this little plateau to test things on before moving on to the big stuff. I need to make sure that the combat and the movement and the sounds and effects and [b]rewards[/b] and other gameplay systems are all polished and """there""" before I continue to expand the scope of the game.

Without taking this time in the "arena shooter" era of the game, I never would have added things like the new staggering system:

https://youtu.be/aBYX1EnwjJw

Or the soon-to-be-implemented executions system (yep, it's finally happening).

There are a lot of things I think GTTOD [b]needs[/b] to have before I really settle in and hammer this bad boy out to turn it into the idea that I've always wanted it to be, but...

[h1]But we're close...really really close...[/h1]

Anyway, onto the next thing.

[previewyoutube=iNjQznGRHwo;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]Really really long YouTube Description[/h1]

So, I had an issue where rewards in GTTOD were too easy to get and far too common around the world. Basically, if you can find good rewards easy-peasy, those rewards loses their "perceived value" and can no longer be used to compensate the player for playing the game. The things that were most negatively affected by this overabundance were:

1. Weapons
2. Extra Lives
3. Health

If you came across any of these three things in GTTOD, you probably just went "Eh" and casually took a look at 'em. They're everywhere, so who cares?

Not to say I'm necessarily going to (I'm totally going to), but if I were to shove you into a room and drop 30 Razors in there with you, you'd ideally want a reward for surviving that, yeah? Well what on Earth can I even give you for that (in the current state of the game)?

Weapons? Why would I? You can get weapons everywhere.

Health? You're probably already full health from healing in that encounter.

Extra Lives? Why would you need that when you hardly ever die?

See what I mean? I can't begin to give you interesting combat engagements if I don't have a adequate way to reward you at the end of it. The best example of this in GTTOD would be the Shrine of the Summit. I think that pretty adequately rewards a player for a heightened state of gameplay (infinite spawning / buffed enemies) by giving you a cool new perk. Or, possibly, even leveling up. You get a cool new Starter Card that may-or-may-not-be-Gunzerker-the-only-good-card and so it's actually totally worth all the trouble.

I should also probably explain that "rewards" don't necessarily have to be things that I give you. A reward for killing a cool boss in games can be anything from a cutscene that reveals an intriguing plot point to a cool new weapon. In this case, a "rewarding" experience is something that would satisfy you in SOME way. So, to me, I really like making crunchy and satisfying effects. So, even though the reward may be something you've experienced before (gaining an extra life); putting that reward in a unique spot that you have to unlock, and then playing a charge effect with satisfying sounds and visuals before BOOM giving them the actual reward makes that reward way way cooler and more sought after. It's a way I can actually compensate you for your hard work. Sure, the rewards haven't changed, functionally. But how you acquire them and what happens once you DO get them is all the difference.

ANYWAY, so these three bunkers are my first steps towards actually solving this problem of overabundance.

The first bunker is the Cargo Bunker. You may have seen this in a previous video. Basically this bunker has a high chance of containing the Grab A Gun, ammo, and weapons. It's also guaranteed to have a Inventory Upgrade station.

The second bunker is the Research Bunker. This bunker has a low chance of containing a Grab A Gun, but a high chance of containing health and shield items. It also has the Altar of Renewal which grants you an extra life.

The third bunker is the Cursed Bunker. This bunker holds practically nothing but points. Points all over the place. You can find it in the water below you, in chests along the bridge, and on the main platform. What's most interesting about THIS bunker, however, is the Curse Stone. This will add a single curse to your character that can influence you in negative ways, BUT it will also grant you a butt-load of points for the trouble. You'll have to play around with it and see how it works out for you. You can only have one curse at a time, and if you make it to the next level with your current curse, you can purify it from you if you find the Curse Stone again.

The bunkers aren't ENTIRELY done yet (the Curse Stone doesn't grant points yet since I wanna get all the curses in game first so I know, on average, what it is ideally worth to the player to gamble with the stone) - but I am definitely getting close to finishing these bad boys off.

Anyway, I'm running out of character space. I ranted far too hard.

See ya!

-Andrew, GTTOD Dev Creature

notes.title: Some big changes coming to GTTOD...
notes.content:
[previewyoutube=8xEuGG9mSN4;full][/previewyoutube]

[h1]YOUTUBE DESCRIPTION[/h1]

So after finishing the last update, I decided there were a few things that needed to change. Here's a quick outline of all the problems I want to address:

1. The first 30 minutes of the game sucks
2. Nothing in the game is important enough to be used as a real reward
3. The game is too easy
4. While enemy variety is good, they don't play different enough
5. Once you find a weapon you like, you only really use THAT weapon
6. The Spider's Nest is a shitty level
7. There aren't enough objectives in the game
8. Clambering is really really shitty
9. Wallrunning isn't always consistent
10. The current run-system is same-y

I have set out to make Sticks and Stones Part 2 to address these issues rather than move on with a full new update. Since the next update, "The Dark Down Under" is the last REAL update for Act 1 of GTTOD - I want to be sure that I get the gameplay loop nailed down and feeling good before moving on to Act 2. SO, that's why there's a Part 2 rather than a full new update.

Also I still want to make a trailer using the Sticks and Stones logo animation. I feel like only using that once was really sad since it turned out so good.

Anyway, so this video goes over how I fixed a few of those issues, but not all of them. I worked a lot on rebalancing weapons and enemies to get a smoother gameplay experience. That is covered pretty well in the video. What I didn't cover much, though, would be around the risk / reward gameplay and giving different aspects of the game more inherent meaning. It goes without saying that if you walk into a room with 500 weapons in it, the value of each weapon is diminished by the other weapons around it. BUT, if you walk into a room with a locked chest with ONE weapon in it, then that weapon suddenly becomes the most valuable thing in the room and can be used as a decent reward for finding and using a key. That kind of mentality is what I've kinda been basing these changes off of.

So yeah, weapons you find in the world will be far more expensive and rare, but you'll also have cheaper weapons that you can buy from the Grab A Gun that will often spawn inside of these new bunkers. You'll still be able to keep an ear out for the Grab A Gun jingle that you can hear through the bunker doors, but getting and using a key on that bunker is where it's really going to come into play. Making weapons rarer also gives me some room to improve them from a general use standpoint. You saw that in this video with the pistol which now functions much more like the Heavy Pistol (which has been removed). It has a much higher damaging projectile than the old pistol, has far more range, and otherwise is much more powerful and useful as a precision weapon.

Moving on from that, one of the big things I'm going to be showing off later (when it is done) is the new prologue to GTTOD. I am not sure if it will make it into Sticks and Stones Part 2, but I really hope it does. It's pretty much going to completely change the first 30 or so minutes of the game. This will also function as the new tutorial. I've also taken time to make some new tool tip UI to be used as in-level tutorials. These have little video screens on them so you don't have to stop and read an entire paragraph just to know what you need to do. These little tooltips will be scattered around the world if you have kept tutorials on.

Outside of that, just fixing and polishing up the general gameplay has gone a long way to improve how GTTOD feels and looks to play. I am not sure how much that has come across in the video, but I'm sure people will notice it when the update launches!

Anyway, that's pretty much it for now! Let me know what you guys think in the comments!

notes.title: GTTOD - The Excessively Late Update Patch Notes
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/d2e262996d5c84009b564e056e378a6423b9be97.png[/img]

https://youtu.be/7B1lDhNs-KM

[h1]Well fuck, it finally happened.[/h1]

Please, humor me for a moment while I talk about the last update - kind of a "short" post mortem on my thoughts on it. You can skip this by looking for where the patch notes actually start.

[h1]PREVIOUS UPDATE POST MORTEM[/h1]

Over the last 6 months I have been working day in and day out trying to craft a better version of the game. With the last update, I think I had a vision for what I wanted, but didn't start on that vision early enough or with a clear enough roadmap forward to fully pull it off. There were a lot of good things in the last update that needed to happen. The new arms and rig for the weapons made it possible to craft higher quality animation and really dig in deep on what makes GTTOD's guns some of the best indie guns out there. The world of The Shatter got fleshed out enough that I could pull out some pretty cool mechanics, like the Shrine of the Summit. The Artstyle became more consistent and easier to look at, making running around actually pleasing to the eye. The sound effects got a lot of attention, and really helps to give that sense of weight to what you are doing - especially when it comes to weapons.

I had a vision for a GTTOD that is the perfect [i]"pick up, put down, pick it up later when I feel like it"[/i] arcade shooter. I never wanted to make a game that demands your attention. I wanted to make something that you go to and say [i]"Hey, that sounds like a nice little breather from my other main shooters, I'll play that for a few hours, unlock some cards, and maybe pick it back up a few weeks or months from now again"[/i]. For that, I wanted to make the game as replayable as I possibly could - but not so much that it becomes frustrating. Obviously when talking about replayability, the first place a lot of developer's minds go to is a rogue like. And, you know, GTTOD was never a stranger to rogue mechanics. The weapons and equipment have always been random, and there have been a few iterations of a rogue mode that have popped up there and again in GTTOD from time to time as I toyed with the idea.

But, I think I went too far down that rabbit hole. I got lost somewhere between [i]"Yeah let's make a challenging video game with replayability"[/i] and [i]"Yeah I love CBT - the video game"[/i]. I had just finished Halo 2 on Legendary when I was making that last update, and I feel like I got sucked into that loop of dying and trying again without really understanding why that worked for Halo 2. As inspired as I am by games like Halo and DOOM, GTTOD is a different beast altogether, and I wasn't looking at that last update from the lens of [i]"What is GTTOD"[/i], but rather from a [i]"What is my pipedream FPS game?"[/i].

When the last update wasn't received well, I really couldn't understand it at first. By that time, after so many months of development, I had played the game so much that I had become an unkillable cheeser, and so the game posed no difficulty to me. I would use that reasoning to pump up the difficulty and make it more and more challenging, since my sights were focused on making a challenging video game for players like me. There's a reason I put so much time into reworking the death effects and animations - it's because I wanted to emphasize it. That, in turn, led me to want to focus a lot on the things around death as well. I wanted to slow the game down to focus more on the combat in the movement, but I did it prematurely since I hadn't quite figured out how to make fun combat yet. The slowing down of the player was a bandaid on my issue of not rewarding players enough for engaging in combat and instead deciding to skip the entire level.

But it goes further than that. Even with slower players, people still just wanted to run. Who knew people wanted to move fast in a parkour game based on Titanfall? Not me, apparently. So I decided to force the issue even more. I implemented a key system for the "teleporter" (not the door, since I was wanting to make the door seem more ethereal and put it in a realm of its own, which is its own stupid side tangent) and locked players into the level. They HAD to fight. I want them to see all my pretty guns and to die to try again and see MORE guns!

[h3]Long story short, what I thought I wanted wasn't actually what I wanted, and even had it been what I wanted, I was no where near the point where I could have pulled it off.[/h3]

[i]The combat was not good enough, the movement was not stable enough, the visuals were not pretty enough, the polish was not shiny enough, and the playerbase was not willing enough.[/i]

[h3]So, back to the drawing board.[/h3]

[h1]The Excessively Late Update Patch Notes:[/h1]

[list]
[*] Expansions on the things that the last update did right, like visuals, audio, and animation
[*] Lots of reworked and completely new weapons to help fill roles in the sandbox
[*] More enemies that move and fight in different ways to increase variety
[*] Blanket rebalances across the board to influence players to WANT to fight, rather than to force them to
[*] A completely new door system that is more forgiving of player error and has more options on how to progress through it, with or without combat
[*] Levels that are longer, more expansive, and filled with more things to do
[*] Removed the upgrade totem in favor of upgrade pick-ups. Faster, less confusing, not random - fair
[*] A new equipment system with equipment more designed to deal damage and assist the player
[*] A new equipment slot so you can carry more than one
[*] An ultimate ability - TIME STOP - that you can charge by engaging in the combat systems
[*] An XP system so you can unlock Starter Cards no matter what mode you're playing in
[*] New starter cards, many of which completely change up how you play the game (try Gunzerker when you unlock it, it's really fun)
[*] A re-emphasis on movement. Speed has increased by a shitload across the board, and using your movement abilities now directly influence how proficient you are in combat
[*] An endless mode with a separate progression system than the main game
[*] New menus and options, which are still in the process of getting reworked (the keybinds is a good example of how I want the other menus to look)
[*] A new level management system that shuffles levels around each time you play, and allows for things like looping runs and levels
[*] Added other level events like ambushes, cargo bunkers, and cycle stones
[*] New, faster level loading that doesn't require a separate loading area
[*] A new, bigger (but very empty) HUB where I have enough room to add cool new things and interactables in later updates
[*] Grab-A-Gun adjustments to turn it into more of a reward for progressing and exploring rather than just a bunch of cheap guns that aren't that good
[*] Bug fixes out the wazoo
[*] HUGE optimizations with regards to performance and stuttering
[/list]

All in all, is this update really that big of a deal? Yeah, I actually think so. I am refocused, and determined to bring you guys the game you want. This is that first step that I have always been trying to make, but never knowing how. This is the foundation for a game I have been looking for, and hopefully for one you've been wanting. It's a stepping stone to further expansion on a, what I think, is a good base. Is it full of content? It's alright. But what's most important is that it's fun, it plays well, it runs well, and there's PLENTY of open space to just add add add add add content left and right.

If you run around The Shatter or the HUB, you can see where I am planning on adding those expansions first. If you beat the Blade Sentinel and look at the world that The Tavern level exists in, you can see where we're going. I really do hope you guys like this update, because this is what I'm doing now. This is the direction I'm heading in, and I'm not slowing down anytime soon. I think this is what is right for the game, and progressing with more levels, more events, more enemies, more guns, more mechanics, and more overall game content is what I'm going to be doing from here on out.

Anyway, toodles! I'll see all of you in the next big GTTOD update slated for mid-August, [b]Sticks and Stones![/b]

During these runs you'll be unlocking new arenas, new levels, and new Starter Cards with modifiers to keep things interesting.

notes.title: UPDATE WHEN? Not sure, but here's the progress I've made in the last few months!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/eebca311feb681be6fed247af61f2d483c779b91.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/60f8539852b2a2514283f2caaba50e791558d0d9.png[/img][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/5e943cb0e317ae46fd0dd8b519c433d83c24cad8.png[/img]

[i]I'M WORKING ON IT! In fact, here's an entire post full of a bunch of the stuff I have been working on over the last few months. Every single aspect about the game has received polish, bug fixing, and new content in droves. I've been working my ass off on this thing, and I really hope this post gets you excited for the updating coming to Steam soon.[/i]

[h1]So, without further ado...[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/c7b33ed455f779ea02b8507886f3d892d05d047e.gif[/img]

[b]I started out this Update Journey with taking a step back and really polishing out how wallrun detection works.[/b] In the current version, I have a handful of raycasts pointing out around the player, and as soon as they detect something, the wall sucks the player in.

This obviously has led to a lot of issues with walls being pretty much magnets, so instead of doing that, I went back and reworked it. Now, wall detection is based on a mixture of player input and directional velocity (which direction the player is moving as well as a cutoff point for when the player is moving fast enough at a particular angle to automatically latch onto a wall without input.)

Here is a video summarizing the changes I made back then with comparisons to Titanfall 2:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5zcmekSx9oU

[b]After that, I wanted to implement a feature I've always wanted to have in GTTOD - CUSTOM WEAPONS.[/b] I wanted to make it so that any player can get a tool package for Unity to make any type of gun they would want for GTTOD. These could be used on custom maps, in every mode, and even be purchased from the Grab-A-Gun vending machines scattered around the map.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/942537c0331fa5c7ceabcb3a2f4f7024d888c77d.png[/img]

[i]I started with the basics, making it so you could create simple weapons.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/51da96fd6c7a4c4a8b914ad961f9541b49f8cdc9.gif[/img]

[i]Eventually, the tools expanded, and things like Halo Gravity Hammers and Bitconnect Guns were possible.[/i]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/14c625c83cc08163f4d8e05ebc99d3c2454cfa1d.gif[/img]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2JfPf8w-wHQ&feature=youtu.be

These tools will be available to the public soon! Right now myself and a few other content creators are going through and testing them out. We've been making some cool weapons and expanding the tools, and you can see a lot of them over in the Discord server!

[b]Next I started working on a shop called the BUILD-A-BANG for the HUB world you start in.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/71ce557de58e62b180f537a2a93a72760b8fac98.gif[/img]

This would allow you to purchase weapons before starting a run. There was a bank located close to the shop, so when you returned from a run you could store your points and use them to buy weapons!

[b]In the end, this is what became of the weapon shop. It turned from a small weapon printer, to an entire shop located in the caves of the HUB![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/3e9b1765e4ef8fb0e2c8ea8fa08a19c5630c5bc4.gif[/img]

[b]Next up was menus.[/b] I redesigned pretty much the entirety of the main menu, making it shift from one location to the next.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/d83e08e7a778a982d20e747f077641d419fe6916.gif[/img]

Now you can more easily swap between modes / the HUB, options, and other parts of the game with the expand tabs on the left of each button. This menu was also designed for all aspect ratios (unlike the last one...sorry about that lol)

After that I began working on some new levels, including the level a lot of you played in the most recent demo! Along with these levels came a few new enemy types like the Grunt, the new Razors, Arachnoturrets, Brutes, Shades, Bruisers, Infantry, Ticks, and Laser Drones.

I don't have gifs of them all and I'm way too lazy to GET a GIF of them all, so here's the grunt and some early screenshots of the level.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/c895a2d0baa5ebb68e6ecabafe29eeec04a7a1ae.gif[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/a9becca9214f968df491dfa7ae134073c721ad76.png[/img]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/9b02aa11c516da816528e5f5a42af6e3f5985fd0.png[/img]

Finally, we laid the original GTTOD pistol (which was the first weapon ever made for the game) to rest and replaced it with a brand new, hot ass handgun.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/3ef30925960bc462285f539511000ab53f0b4476.gif[/img]

I did end up sending the pistol off with a funeral video on the YT channel though...

https://youtu.be/iOP09NjD-FQ

[b]After that I started working on the things you'd be doing IN those levels.[/b] Things like exploring, looting, and interacting with the environment. The first thing I did was add in ammo counters and methods to acquire ammo. Weapons were split up between different ammo types, and you could get this ammo by looting chests, crates, trash cans, and ammo tubes - as well as killing enemies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/d644a1d0cd19a4371952c0b1f54f6bb9240d3bae.gif[/img]

[b]Once these were added, I wanted to give players a way to more easily collect these items.[/b] This led me to make the "Pull" ability. With this, you could hold down the melee button to pull all physics objects close into you. This also includes things like crates, health, and even enemies (it staggers them).

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/a1726a19b3432a40499fb86faa775613a6188979.gif[/img]

[b]Next up I started working on some new movement abilities and items. The first two was the grappling hook and the rocket block![/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/333a5682c56d01764de1a156a5f757122f718729.gif[/img]

https://youtu.be/ZJVsE9-OaTc

After this I finished implementing things like swimming, dash resetting, triple jumping, dash canceling, better sliding mechanics, swing poles, rail grinding, and a bunch of other shit.

[b]Also new BHG.[/b]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=FS6YA8NPfV8&feature=youtu.be

[h1]At this point in time I'm gonna skip forward a few months because I'm tired of going through all the announcements in my Discord server and Papa Johns is going to be here in five minutes and I want to find a stopping point for the night (:[/h1]

I know a good place to start up again...

How about the time I got a brand new rig for the game, and had to redo every single animation one after another - pretty much from scratch?

Here's what I have to say about that:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/226eb2618784866cae484806949a5eab457b377e.png[/img]

[b]This huge change in the character, with new hands and fingers, resulted in the biggest killing-off of weapons the game had ever seen.[/b] The weapon count went from 32 to 14 in a day...and it was the best thing that could have happened.

Over the next few months, I went through and remade all the equipment, all the guns, all the animations, all the cutscenes...everything. And the new stuff looks fantastic. With the help of a few animator friends, we turned the game around to look and feel better than ever. I implemented new tools for the weapon system for more indepth animation states and camera shake settings, new types of weapons like heat-based and new charge systems, and TONS more. The weapons that are in game now are better than they've ever been.

[b]After a few months of work, the weapon count went from 14, and now rests at a very happy 35.[/b] Not only did I redo every single one of the weapons and improve them in every single way, but I even added brand new weapons. I can't wait for you to get a chance to use them all - really, I'm super proud of all of them. GTTOD has some badass weapons and equipment.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/b329b08f106c02bad532db2f16561a2a1cc533ac.gif[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/e2d77308256c6d27635d1a78b51130edf41d77e1.gif[/img]
(Also this is a boss fight template thing I made on a live stream lol)

[b]To go along with all these new weapons, I finalized my design for the weapon wheel, and got it fully implemented.[/b]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/28583292/c7354e338c933725e3a9e1cbcac16d5053fa9f97.gif[/img]

[h1]So, what's next?[/h1]
[i]Lol hell if I know, I just work here.[/i]

Right now I am working on some new levels, new art, new music, new enemies, and trying my best to tie everything together into a final product for all of you to enjoy. I know it has been a long time since the last update, but because of that time I think I have set some expectations for myself that I fully intend to fulfill. By the end of this update, I want the game to be smooth and polished and relatively bug free. I want it to be a full experience with depth and content. I want to have the tools ready to build a strong modding community, and I'd like to be at the head of that community guiding the way (at least to the best of my ability).

These things take time, and I hope that you guys are still around by the time I get it all sorted out. Thanks so much for sticking with me through these long update droughts! I promise the end game will be worth it.

[h2]Oh yeah also new trailer.[/h2]

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YjftEVv82Uk

Thanks for reading and watching everyone! My pizza is here and I want to go eat, so I'm going to abruptly end this off. I'll see you all later!

[h1]LADIES AND GENTLEMEN, IT'S THE GTTOD SHOWWWWW[/h1]

While I may not have a TV show set that I can savagely tear down, I do have a community to shitpost to and shove a load of content down their throats!

Welcome back everyone! It's been a hot second since we've last spoke! I hope you are all doing well, and I hope you are ready for an absolute load's worth of GTTOD to be served into your lives. Without further ado, lets blow this popsicle stand.

[b]After I got back home from Boston, I immediately got to work trying to capture a new visual style for GTTOD that better represented what I wanted out of the game.[/b]

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28583292/5c3fd90aa6dc6138d1f11de244185978b6ac2ba0.png[/img]

https://gfycat.com/incompleteamplebubblefish

I played around with the idea of doing some sick glory kills to gain back slowmo and health. Although the future of this mechanic is unknown, I did really like how it played!

https://youtu.be/X10sTxc3Txs

I decided that GTTOD's health system needed another looking at as well (you probably saw this in the UI image up there). GTTOD's health system is now more of a mixture of Halo Reach and Bloodborne. Your base shield can be melted right off you, but your "true health" has i-frames to prolong your suffering in low-health situations. Getting kills heals your true health, but only time away from damage can replenish your shield.

https://youtu.be/5nRI7SqtECU

I went back to my roots and began exploring the idea of setting the base levels out on slightly-randomly-generated buildings and rooftops. Suddenly the visuals for GTTOD began to REALLY take shape, and a theme began to emerge.

https://gfycat.com/clutteredembellishedgoose

https://gfycat.com/rapidashamedalaskajingle-arcade-coin-gaming

https://gfycat.com/illustriousoddkillerwhale

I also decided to re-visit the idea of staggering and dodging enemies. It went well, and a new dodge effect and ability was gifted onto the Dereks.

https://youtu.be/GVDpeVsQYk0

https://gfycat.com/hilariousactualarawana

https://gfycat.com/crazysphericalanaconda

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28583292/5e71640af0134a20863e546679c8567e8e6764f3.png[/img]

With the new style, a new HUB island was born, replacing the long lost island from the Over-Overhaul.

https://gfycat.com/madsilverhalcyon-rocketleague

The HUB world became the center of a new, expanded ravine. Falling into the ravine became a start of a new area for GTTOD.

[b]The ABYSS[/b]

A deep and dark cavern where a sleeping city waits. You are stranded down here, and there is no escape. This is GTTOD's new endless mode.

https://gfycat.com/grimypowerlessfruitfly

https://gfycat.com/fearlesscostlybedlingtonterrier-pcmasterrace-video-games-game-dev-parkour-gttod

[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28583292/b75bcc8353cbe49fe9312743d384893abb2bdf2b.jpg[/img]

And that concludes this month's content dump. If you've made it this far, then I guess all I have to say is this:

GTTOD will be re-released into Early Access at the end of May. That's a promise.

I will see you all there!

Toodles!

notes.title: I have taken GTTOD off the Steam Store temporarily
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28583292/ee4a057a0471afe994e8dc827d8de5461bd925fc.png[/img]

I know this may not be the BEST announcement for this time of year, but this decision did not come easily.

So to catch you up on what has been happening the last 6 months:


[h1]6 months ago, GTTOD's files became corrupted[/h1]

A bunch of issues started popping up. The game began to break down due to an asset I was using not being updated to work with newer versions of Unity. This caused a HUGE corruption of code in the game, and lead to things like the BSOD in Legacy GTTOD.

[h1]GTTOD got a redesign[/h1]

For a while I tried to hold onto it, but I realized that the direction GTTOD was heading in wasn't a good one. It was generic. Part of what made me realize this was talking to publishers, one in particular who really told me what was up. I decided to redesign GTTOD from scratch with NO assets, and to focus on what makes GTTOD unique and stand out.

[h1]I released a beta version of the new GTTOD[/h1]

It went pretty well! Lots of new players, new sales, new fans, everything was going great! However due to how complex I made the character controller, levels had to be BIGGER and BETTER and more AWESOME than ever. This made developing for GTTOD a lot slower.

[h1]I decided GTTOD didn't have enough content at the moment to be worth the price[/h1]

This was the tough decision. I took a look at the game that I had on Steam and I compared it to the amount of content that I had in legacy. The new content was amazing, polished, played well, looked well, and was overall better than ANYTHING in legacy. However there just wasn't enough of it.

[h1]I took GTTOD off Steam to further development until I feel it has enough content[/h1]

So for those of you who purchased the game, you still can play it and I will still update it regularly! However I just don't want to sell the game to people anymore if I can't give them at least a semi realized game.

I need to make more levels, modes, weapons, and enemies before I am comfortable selling GTTOD. When I do come back I will put GTTOD back on sale again for those of you who missed the Winter Sale. It will also have a TON of new content and polish, and I will make SURE it will be worth more than the $10 I am selling it for.

This was a tough decision but I made it because I value my name. I value being someone who doesn't screw people over, and I didn't think selling GTTOD with so little content stood up to that sentiment. I will be back soon!

Sorry for the inconvenience.

-Andrew, GTTOD Dev

notes.title: GTTOD: Over-overhaul patch notes
notes.content:
[img]https://steamcdn-a.akamaihd.net/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28583292/a80e742e8345e3e3586f4c5ecf43e483f10b83e8.png[/img

Wow that took a long time.

After three months of work, I can happily say that the Over-overhaul is FINISHED. I have gone through and completely re-made a huge portion of the game, and right now I could not be more satisfied. If you are seeing this and HAVEN'T checked out the new stuff, what the hell are you doing? Get in there and give it another shot!

To everyone who sat through the last three months, thank you so much for your support. I hope that where the game is now satisfies you, since it's only going to get better from here.

The positive reviews I have been getting have really filled me with determination to keep working and keep going, and I thank all of you so so much for writing them. We are almost at 90% positive! HYPE!

ANNNNYWAY, lets get these patch notes over with so I can get back to making the game, and you guys can get back to enjoying your Saturday.

[list]
    [*] Six new levels
    [*] Added water where there at one point was nothing
    [*] Swimming
    [*] Enemy teleportation
    [*] Enemy tweaks
    [*] Optimization
    [*] Real lighting and shadows
    [*] All new art and art direction
    [*] New menus, options, and level selects
    [*] All new weapons, weapon tweaks, and animation fixes
    [*] New bullet effects
    [*] New enemies (turrets, new Sword and Kamikaze enemies)
    [*] New trailer!
    [*] Launch pads
    [*] Dash resets
    [*] New momentum-based parkour system
    [*] Parkour tweaks and fixes
    [*] Over-all bug fixes (literally hundreds, I'm not listing that shit)
    [*] New race mode based on 10 second timer
    [*] New Ninja mode with updated sword mechanics
    [*] New tutorial
    [*] Work on a save system
    [*] Dialogue system
    [*] Started work on the actual story of the game in new intro
    [*] Probably a lot more but I'm tired of listing things
[/list]

I think the real bummer is that this isn't even all I have worked on over the last three months. There are still a TON of new things that I haven't even put in the game yet, and are just waiting to be implemented. I won't be putting them in until more levels are added to the rotation, that way I don't cram pack the current levels and cause a really bad "Indie" difficulty curve (thanks for the wording, Ven). As time passes and more content is added to the game, I will be working with this difficulty curve a lot.

So, for now, enjoy the update, and I'll see you all in the next one!

-Andrew

PS: Don't forget to join the discord to catch up on what is really going down on a daily basis, and to also report bugs and add in suggestions!

notes.title: GTTOD Update 2 -Hordes'n'such-
notes.content:
[url=http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28583292/8ee42b11607409c63598567208614e4a95ea70c2.jpg][img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28583292/5408a2afe3dd990c7d7a1bc666a4a3b7a3735e68.jpg[/img][/url][img]http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28583292/8ee42b11607409c63598567208614e4a95ea70c2.jpg[/img]

Christ this took forever. The update will be out in a few minutes. Taking an extra look and tweaking Emission a bit.

Lots and lots and LOTS of changes here in this update, many of which I have probably already forgotten. I never ever want to take three weeks working on one update again. I feel like I have burned my retinas out staring at this computer for this long. At this point, I am probably gonna focus fire on some bugs for the next week or two to get the game to a more stable point, as well as adding some more things to Arena and Horde mode to fill them out a bit, but I will focus more on that after I get through these patch notes.

Here we go:

[h1]IMA BIG ASS THING OF PATCH NOTES RIGHT HERE[/h1]

[list]
    [*]Added a new mode, HORDE MODE
    [*]Added the ability to run straight up walls
    [*]Overhauled Ninja mode. New block and ranged attacks
    [*]New enemy type, the Sword Dude
    [*]New Grab-A-Gun art, as well as more of them
    [*]Brand new tutorial embedded in the levels. Enabled in the Default mode!
    [*]Fixed level 11, it works now.
    [*]Fixed Arena Mode, it also works now
    [*]Brand new level 10. Yep, the last one is gone now.
    [*]Added melee enemies to Arena Mode
    [*]New weapon, Felony
    [*]New starter pistol, Larceny v_2
    [*]Updated collisions and z-fighting on buildings
    [*]Fixed clambering bugs so you will no longer get stuck
    [*]Added new sounds for wall running
    [*]Footstep system! You are no longer a silent ghost!
    [*]Fixed enemies with tons of health after dying
    [*]Sped up some reloads with new sounds
    [*]Second page on the main menu (nothing too crazy)
    [*]More optimization changes
    [*]You now have to be firmly planted on a wall before you jump off.
    [*]Increased dash cooldown to lessen spam
    [*]Potential fix for the -10 health, staying alive thing
    [*]Lowered volume on music and other sound effects
    [*]Player now walks slightly faster
    [*]Improved head bob and directional head bob
    [*]Made level 11 a tad bit less bullshit
    [*]Fixed some weapons flying through your face when you fall
[/list]

And I did a lot more, but like I said I have the memory of an electric toothbrush so I really can't say what I missed. I guess we will find out later when the FBI breaks my front door down to let me know I suck at making video games.

Heh.

Anyway, moving on, I will be focusing a LOT on some bug fixes and little tweaks for the next week, but all that kind of stuff is really boring. Lets talk about the fun stuff.

I have started working on the next big update, which will be the Weapons Update. Despite it's name, there will be a LOT more than just weapons in it, and I'll talk about it a little.

Every single weapon in the game is going to be getting a fresh new coat of paint. You can kinda see the start of this with the new starter pistol and Felony. Your muzzle flash is now attached to the weapon, as well as the gun not flying through your face. On top of that, they have new animations (done by me, so they still kinda suck). I will be hiring on an animator to help me out a little bit. He can make it look pretty while I update the functionality of weapons.

Some weapons will be totally redone, like the Shotgun and Assault. I think these need the most attention. I will also be getting around to fixing the weapon-animation-stick bug with the Affray and Breaking and Entering pistols. I know how to fix it, they just haven't been a huge priority with the whole game falling apart last update and such.

But, enough about weapons, what else is gonna be in the next update?

Well, glad I asked, me! Thanks for asking!

I will be pushing v_2 of Arena Mode and Horde Mode in the next update. This will add lots of new cool shit to the maps of these game modes, adding more functionality, and improving on what they currently are in general. This means a better buying-system, more objectives, better weapons, and just generally improving the flow of the game.

More so than that, will be the Settings Menu overhaul I have been talking about for weeks. A full key-rebinding system as well as better options in general.

I think I have promised one guy that the inverted mouse would be in the last two updates, and yet I keep letting him down. I may go and add that in while I am fixing bugs in the next few days.

If you are reading this, I am so sorry. I have some left-overs from Thanksgiving if you want them? P-please don't hate me.

Moving on from that update, is the big dog. The one and only. The moment we have all been waiting for.

The Rogue Lite update. I have talked about this extensively. The rogue lite mode has been in development since about 5 months ago, which is a really long time considering that GTTOD, in it's entirety, has been in development for 19 months.

A regular mode, like Horde mode or Emission, generally take about 1 month to get to v_1. Rogue lite has taken 5 times that amount, and still isn't even half way. I will be working on Rogue Lite a BUNCH after the next two rounds of bug fixes and the Weapons Update is done.

This will probably be the biggest update GTTOD will ever see. I simply do not know how I will be able to top it after Rogue Lite is done. It will easily triple if not quadruple the size of the game.

However, I will talk more about that after the next update.

I have a lot of work to do, and a lot of bullshit cut out for me.

I hope this update can suffice until I get more work done. Thanks for sticking with me and dealing with my lack of updates recently. I love you guys, fo real.

Have fun!

-Andrew
